Azure Government note: Incremental refresh is Verify for Gov for Service execution. Validate license, workspace, gateway, source, and cloud support before making policy setup required.

This model already has the Desktop-side prerequisites in place, built in Lab 03:
1. RangeStart and RangeEnd are DateTime parameters defined in Power Query (expressions.tmdl), currently set to 2026-01-01 / 2026-04-01.
2. The FactOrders partition query filters on OrderDate using [OrderDate] >= Date.From(RangeStart) and [OrderDate] < Date.From(RangeEnd) — see the FilteredByRefreshRange step.
3. Archive/refresh window (example policy): archive 2 years of history, refresh the most recent 1 month, with a 1-day incremental detect-changes granularity.
4. Detect data changes: not configured in this training model since FactOrders has no LastModified/ETL timestamp column; if the source provided one, it would be referenced in the Detect data changes column setting.
5. Service prerequisites to validate before publishing: Premium/Fabric capacity or Pro-eligible workspace, a supported data source and (if applicable) gateway, and that the RangeStart/RangeEnd parameters are recognized by the Incremental refresh dialog (Modeling > Incremental refresh) after publish.

This exercise is a review, not a build — the table below shows the same OrderDate-filtered FactOrders rows the incremental refresh policy would apply against.
